envelope.author: nico
envelope.reason: a guard that refuses every stop with no bound loops the session forever; Claude Code's Stop hook carries stop_hook_active for exactly this, and guard-precision removed the bound while the ruling was held
envelope.cause: decision note 'turn-end guard waves a refused stop through on retry'; guard-precision closed

payload.gloss: a guard binds exactly the agents whose composition includes it, and only in such an agent’s own main session, never in a subagent it dispatches, which is bounded by what it was handed, judged by its assay and the whole check, and supervised by the main session; on every supported harness it judges every turn it fires on; where its judge cannot run, it lets the turn through and says so, never silently, and it asks the judge again once the judge may have recovered, so a passing outage never leaves the guard unjudged for the rest of a session. A judgement fits within the time its harness allows a guard, so a judge that is merely slow is never reported as one that could not run. A guard judges an act against the contract of the agent that performs it, and a refused act stays refused however often it is retried: a retry is judged again, never waved through. What a guard hands its judge is only what its one decision needs, the test stated in a few sentences and the act and contract it applies to, because every sentence beyond that costs time and gives the judge more to misread. Where a harness cannot tell which agent is running, the guard is carried as a stated rule instead and the operator is told; a guard that fires and judges nothing never ships. The turn end is the one exception: refusing it holds back no effect, it only makes the agent redo its turn, so the turn-end guard may let a repeated or several-times-refused stop through, saying so, rather than lock a session in an endless loop.
